items.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: my teacher was the Executive Director, Penny Phillips. So I was involved with performing in concerts there and also with the Connecticut Classical Guitar Society guitar ensemble

ctx.x: What kind of outlet did you have to perform the classical guitar music?

Well I took lessons for ten years at Community Music School Springfield, so they had recitals every year that you could perform in, and they had combos. I had — one year it was two recorders and guitar, another year it was four guitars. So that was nice to be able to have a variety of ensembles to play with. And also the Connecticut Classical Guitar Society, that was based in West Hartford, my teacher was the Executive Director, Penny Phillips. So I was involved with performing in concerts there and also with the…
This whole thing about becoming a professional, about playing gigs, showing up on time, all that knowing what’s appropriate in the different gigs, I think you probably got pretty early then.
